deviations.reason: exactOptionalPropertyTypes and noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature are off so the upstream Feishu source compiles verbatim: OpenClaw own tsconfig sets neither flag.
The extension private runtime barrel re-exports ~30 members of the OpenClaw plugin host. Only the members the ported files read are declared, sourced from @getpaseo/channels-core.
The status-sink contract upstream declares inside the omitted monitor.ts.
The durable-invoker contract upstream declares inside the omitted feishu-ingress.ts; the Hub owns the durable queue.

The inbound download half of the omitted media.ts, with upstream function name, parameters and response-shape ladder, over a Hub-supplied per-account download directory instead of the OpenClaw media store.
Upstream stores the plugin runtime in OpenClaw global plugin runtime store; the Hub injects it through src/fusion/runtime.ts. Accessor names and the throw-on-unset contract are unchanged.

Upstream runs one account per process, so one slot holds the runtime. The Hub runs every account of every organization in one process, so the runtime is keyed by account id and the account travels in AsyncLocalStorage.

Partial port: the three resolveFeishu*IngressAccess resolvers and their ingress identity/subject helpers are omitted because they run OpenClaw channel-ingress-runtime (the src/channels/message-access admission subsystem). The Hub owns inbound admission, DM/group policy and allowlists (goal slice 23). Everything the read policy and reply policy need is kept line for line.

Upstream fetchWithSsrFGuard sits on OpenClaw pinned-dispatcher stack. This keeps the call contract plus the hostname-suffix allowlist and the private-address block; per-hop redirect re-validation, DNS pinning and proxy dispatcher policies are not carried.

Upstream resolves an account from OpenClaw process-wide config.json plus FEISHU_* env fallbacks. The Hub compiles the config revision and passes two carriers; the env fallbacks are deliberately not carried because a Hub process serves every organization.
Installs the ported FeishuPluginRuntime over HostRuntime keyed stores, the vertical SSRF-guarded fetch and a per-account media directory, replacing OpenClaw SQLite state dir and host media services.
Normalizes a Lark event into the shared ChannelInboundEvent instead of running the omitted monitor.message-handler turn pipeline. Content, mention and chat-type decisions come from the ported source.
Registers the Lark EventDispatcher handlers over the shared inbound processor and rebuilds upstream durable/non-durable invoker contract on top of the Hub queue.
Seam that builds the dispatcher and runs the ported monitorWebSocket; the reconnect loop itself is upstream.
Seam that builds the dispatcher and runs the ported monitorWebhook with the durable invoker; signature verification, challenge handling and the guards are upstream.

Upstream registers the six feishu_* tool families through the OpenClaw plugin host registerFull(api). Fusion has no plugin host, so this builds the slice of that API the entry points touch over a Fusion registrar; schemas, descriptions and executors are untouched.
The startAccount seam replacing the omitted monitor.ts fan-out: resolve account, install runtime, probe identity, register the inbound processor, run the configured transport until abort.
Bridges the Hub plugin.outbound contract onto the ported send entry points; all wire decisions stay in send.ts.

Upstream declares the message-action adapter inline in the omitted channel.ts. The action set, target aliases, action gate and per-action argument names are kept over the ported API functions; actions that need the OpenClaw outbound delivery adapter (upload-file, sticker, presentation fallback) are refused rather than advertised.
